intro: Le Guerno is a small Morbihan village built around the Parc animalier et botanique de Branféré, a zoo and botanical garden, and the plane tree at its centre is why some visitors come specifically. Planted roughly 300 years ago, its weeping branches sag to the ground, take root and grow back upward, so the tree has built itself a ring of living arches, the heaviest now resting on metal props. Officially classified a remarkable tree by the French forestry office, its trunk measures four and a half metres round.

trees.name: The Weeping Plane of Branféré
trees.species: Oriental Plane (Platanus orientalis), described in sources as "platane pleureur d'Orient" (weeping form)

location.address: Parc animalier et botanique de Branféré, Kerouar, 56190 Le Guerno, Morbihan, France

trees.access: Paid entry: the tree stands inside the Parc animalier et botanique de Branféré, a working zoo and botanical park in Le Guerno (Morbihan). A visitor needs a park ticket (adult and child pricing, seasonal hours per branfere.com; exact price not independently fetched so not quoted here) to reach it, which is the paid-entry case under hard rule 10, clearly stated rather than hidden.
trees.transport: Rural Morbihan, no rail; nearest towns are Muzillac and La Roche-Bernard, each a short drive away. A car is the realistic way to reach it; not walkable from a station.
trees.story:
The branches of this plane sag until they touch the ground, root where they land and grow back upward, so the tree has built itself a set of arches to stand in. The heaviest limbs have needed metal crutches under them all the same. The crown now spans about 40 metres and shades something like 700 square metres, which is an orchard's worth of cover from one trunk.

It is an oriental plane of the weeping form, put in during the 18th century and so roughly 300 years old, classified a remarkable tree by the French forestry office. The one figure worth a caveat is the trunk. The dendrologist who recorded it gives 4.50 metres circumference; a tourism account of visiting the tree calls 4.5 metres the diameter. A plane 4.5 metres thick would be extraordinary, 4.5 metres round is entirely ordinary at that age, and the circumference reading is the one taken here.

The tree stands inside the Parc animalier et botanique de Branfere, a zoo and botanical garden at Le Guerno, so a ticket and the park's opening hours sit between a visitor and the trunk. People go for it specifically regardless: the local tourist office publishes a piece that is simply somebody's account of setting out to find it. Photographs taken in August 2023 show it standing and in full leaf.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the weeping limbs that reach the ground, root there and grow back up, and by the metal props under the heaviest of them. It stands in the Branfere park at Le Guerno, under a crown about 40 metres across.
